# Yuku, a JavaScript/TypeScript Compiler Toolchain in Zig

> Yuku is a JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.
> Full documentation, every page concatenated for LLMs. Index: https://yuku.fyi/llms.txt

# Introduction

Source: https://yuku.fyi/

Yuku is a JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig, for use from Zig and from JavaScript.

[Try it in the playground →](https://playground.yuku.fyi)

## Why Yuku

**Correct.** Zero failures and zero AST mismatches across the [test suite](https://yuku.fyi/testing/).

**Fast.** Built for speed, see [Performance](#performance).

**Anywhere.** Runs in Node.js, Bun, Deno, Workers, and browsers, see [JavaScript](#javascript).

**Zero dependencies.** Pure Zig, with no dependencies in the build or on npm.

**Modern.** Supports new and proposed syntax, including decorators, source phase and deferred imports, and `using` declarations.

---

> **About these docs**
>These pages cover each part of Yuku and its API, in JavaScript and in Zig. The [source](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src) has the rest.

## Install

### JavaScript

```bash
npm install yuku
```

| Import                                          | For                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| [`yuku`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/#javascript)                   | Parse to an ESTree / TypeScript-ESTree AST        |
| [`yuku/analyzer`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/#javascript) | Resolve scopes, bindings, references, and imports |
| [`yuku/ast`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#javascript)           | Walk, build, and check an AST                     |
| [`yuku/codegen`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/#javascript)   | Print an AST back to source, with source maps     |
| [`yuku/types`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#javascript)         | TypeScript types for the AST                      |

It runs in Node.js 14.18 or newer, Bun, Deno, Workers, and browsers.

### Zig

```bash
zig fetch --save git+https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku.git
```

```zig
// build.zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
my_module.addImport("parser", yuku.module("parser"));
```

Yuku needs Zig 0.17.0 or later.

## Performance

Measured against the alternatives doing the same work, on an Apple M3.

### Parser

Parsing natively, Yuku is faster than Oxc and SWC.

![Parsing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) natively · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-native)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-native/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript.png "Native benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, and SWC parsing typescript.js")

On npm, Yuku parses faster than the alternatives.

![Parsing `react.js` (72 KB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/react.png "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, SWC, Babel, and Acorn parsing react.js")

The lead holds on large files.

![Parsing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript.png "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, SWC, Babel, and Acorn parsing typescript.js")

### Analyzer

Analyzing a whole codebase, resolving every reference and linking every import across files, Yuku is faster than typescript-eslint and the TypeScript API.

![Analyzing three.js (755 files) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/three.png "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, TypeScript, and typescript-eslint analyzing three.js")

The lead holds on a single large file.

![Analyzing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript_js.png "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, TypeScript, and typescript-eslint analyzing typescript.js")

# Parser

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/

The parser turns JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSX into an [AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/). It recovers from errors, so a parse with diagnostics still returns a tree of everything it could read.

## JavaScript

```js
import { parse } from "yuku";

const { program, comments, diagnostics } = parse("const x = 1 + 2;");
```

`parse` takes a string or UTF-8 bytes, and `program` is an [ESTree / TypeScript-ESTree AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#javascript).

### Options

```js
parse(source, { path: "src/app.tsx" });
```

| Option           | Values                                    | Default    | Description                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`           | a file path                               | none       | Names the file in diagnostics. `lang` and `sourceType` default from its extension.         |
| `lang`           | `"js"`, `"jsx"`, `"ts"`, `"tsx"`, `"dts"` | `"js"`     | The syntax to parse, by default from the extension of `path`.                              |
| `sourceType`     | `"module"`, `"script"`, `"commonjs"`      | `"module"` | `"commonjs"` allows top-level `return`, and is the default for `.cjs` and `.cts` paths.    |
| `preserveParens` | `true`, `false`                           | `true`     | Keep `ParenthesizedExpression` nodes.                                                      |
| `semanticErrors` | `true`, `false`                           | `false`    | Also report the early errors that need scopes, such as redeclarations.                     |
| `attachComments` | `true`, `false`                           | `false`    | Also attach each comment to its node, see [Comments](#js-comments).                        |
| `tokens`         | `true`, `false`                           | `false`    | Keep every token, see [Tokens](#js-tokens).                                                |
| `wasm`           | a `WebAssembly.Module`                    | bundled    | A custom build of Yuku, such as one with a [dialect](https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/#javascript).         |

An unknown `lang` or `sourceType` throws a `TypeError`. `langFromPath(path)` and `sourceTypeFromPath(path)` return the values a path implies.

### Result

```ts
interface ParseResult {
  program: Program;
  comments: Comment[];
  tokens?: TokenList; // with tokens: true
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[];
}
```

### Diagnostics

Every part of `yuku` reports diagnostics in this shape.

```ts
interface Diagnostic {
  severity: "error" | "warning" | "hint" | "info";
  message: string;
  path: string | null; // the path option
  start: number;       // UTF-16 offsets, like nodes
  end: number;
  labels: { start: number; end: number; message: string }[];
  help: string | null;
}
```

### Comments

`comments` lists every comment in source order.

```js
const { comments } = parse(`// a line comment\nconst x = 1; /* a block comment */`);
// [
//   { type: "Line", value: " a line comment", start: 0, end: 17 },
//   { type: "Block", value: " a block comment ", start: 31, end: 52 },
// ]
```

`attachComments: true` also attaches each comment to the node next to it, as `node.comments`. [`yuku/codegen`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/#js-comments) prints comments from there, so they move with their nodes.

```js
const { program } = parse(`// header\nfunction foo() {} // trailing`, { attachComments: true });

program.body[0].comments;
// [
//   { type: "Line", position: "before", sameLine: false, value: " header" },
//   { type: "Line", position: "after", sameLine: true, value: " trailing" },
// ]
```

`position` is `"before"`, `"after"`, or `"inside"` an otherwise empty node, such as `function f() { /* hi */ }`.

### Tokens

`tokens: true` keeps every token in a `TokenList`, where a token is an index.

```js
import { parse, TokenKind } from "yuku";

const { tokens } = parse(source, { tokens: true });

for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) {
  if (tokens.kind(i) === TokenKind.Arrow) console.log(tokens.start(i), tokens.text(i));
}
```

```js
tokens.kind(i)                      // one of TokenKind
tokens.text(i)                      // its source text
tokens.start(i)                     // UTF-16 offsets
tokens.end(i)

tokens.isKeyword(i)
tokens.isReserved(i)                // reserved unconditionally or in strict mode
tokens.isUnconditionallyReserved(i)
tokens.isStrictModeReserved(i)
tokens.isIdentifierLike(i)          // an identifier or any keyword
tokens.isNumericLiteral(i)
tokens.isBinaryOperator(i)
tokens.isLogicalOperator(i)
tokens.isUnaryOperator(i)
tokens.isAssignmentOperator(i)
tokens.precedence(i)                // operator precedence, 0 when none

tokens.newlineBefore(i)             // what ASI reads
tokens.escaped(i)
tokens.invalidEscape(i)             // a template chunk whose cooked value is undefined
tokens.loneSurrogate(i)

tokens.range(node)                  // [from, to) of the tokens inside a node
tokens.first(node)
tokens.last(node)
tokens.before(nodeOrOffset)         // the last token ending at or before it
tokens.after(nodeOrOffset)          // the first token starting at or after it
tokens.at(offset)                   // the token containing an offset
```

The queries return an index, or `-1` when there is none. Tokens are as the parser resolved them, so a regex is one `RegexLiteral`, and comments are not tokens. [tokens.ts](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/packages/yuku/types/tokens.ts) lists the kinds.

## Zig

```zig
const std = @import("std");
const parser = @import("parser");

pub fn main() !void {
    var tree = try parser.parse(std.heap.smp_allocator, "const x: number = 1;", .{ .lang = .ts });
    defer tree.deinit();

    for (tree.diagnostics.items) |d| {
        std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{d.message});
    }
}
```

`parse` returns a `Tree` holding the AST, its diagnostics, and the source, and fails only with `error.OutOfMemory`. Everything lives in one arena, so `tree.deinit()` frees it all at once. The tree borrows `source`, which must outlive it. [AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#zig) shows how to read it.

## Options

| Field             | Default   | Description                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source_type`     | `.module` | `.script`, `.module` (strict, with `import` and `export`), or `.commonjs` (top-level `return`) |
| `lang`            | `.js`     | `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, or `.dts`                                                        |
| `preserve_parens` | `true`    | Keep `parenthesized_expression` nodes, or only their inner expression                          |
| `comments`        | `.flat`   | `.none`, `.flat`, `.attached`, or `.both`, see [Comments](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#comments)               |
| `tokens`          | `false`   | Keep every token, see [Tokens](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#tokens)                                            |
| `dialect`         | `false`   | Read the source with the [dialect](https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/) compiled into the parser                  |

`.fromPath` infers `source_type` and `lang` from a file name, as in `.lang = .fromPath("app.tsx")`.

## Diagnostics

The parser reports a syntax error and parses on past it.

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, "const a = 1;\nlet x = ;\nconst y = 2;", .{});
// one diagnostic, "Unexpected token ';'", and a tree holding `a` and `y`
```

Every part of Yuku reports diagnostics in one shape, `ast.Diagnostic`: a `severity` of `.error`, `.warning`, `.hint`, or `.info`, a `message`, a byte `span`, `labels` pointing at related code, and optional `help`.

```zig
for (tree.diagnostics.items) |d| {
    std.debug.print("[{s}] {s} at {d}..{d}\n", .{
        d.severity.toString(), d.message, d.span.start, d.span.end,
    });
    if (d.help) |help| std.debug.print("  help: {s}\n", .{help});
}
```

`tree.hasErrors()` tells whether any error occurred, and `tree.hasDiagnostics()` whether anything was reported. [Semantic analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) adds the early errors that need scopes, such as duplicate `let` declarations and `break` outside a loop.

# AST

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/

The parser produces an AST. In JavaScript it is an ESTree / TypeScript-ESTree tree of plain objects, and in Zig a flat tree in one arena.

## JavaScript

The tree is [ESTree](https://github.com/estree/estree) for JavaScript and JSX, as [Acorn](https://www.npmjs.com/package/acorn) produces it, and [TypeScript-ESTree](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree) for TypeScript, matching [Oxc](https://oxc.rs) for both. It also carries stage 3 [decorators](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-decorators), the `phase` of [import defer](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-defer-import-eval) and [import source](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-source-phase-imports) on imports and `ImportExpression`, and `Program.hashbang`.

`yuku/types` has the TypeScript types of every node, comment, diagnostic, and token, listed in its [type definitions](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/packages/yuku/types/index.ts). `yuku` re-exports them, and a [dialect](https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/#javascript) adds its nodes to them.

```ts
import type { Expression, Identifier, Node, Statement } from "yuku";
```

`yuku/ast` walks, builds, and checks the tree, and works on an ESTree AST from any parser.

### Walking

```js
import { parse } from "yuku";
import { walk } from "yuku/ast";

const { program } = parse(source);

walk(program, {
  Identifier(node) {
    console.log(node.name);
  },
  CallExpression: {
    enter(node, ctx) {},
    leave(node, ctx) {},
  },
  Function(node) {
    // function declarations, expressions, and arrows
  },
  enter(node) {},
});
```

Handlers are keyed by node `type`, by alias group, or by the universal `enter` / `leave`, and receive the exact node type. The alias groups are `Expression`, `Statement`, `Declaration`, `ModuleDeclaration`, `Function`, `Class`, `Method`, `Loop`, `Pattern`, `JSX`, and `TSType`. Per node, the order is the universal `enter`, alias enters, the typed enter, the children, then the same in reverse for leave.

An optional third argument passes state to every handler as `ctx.state`. `walkAsync` walks in the same order and awaits every handler. [`module.walk`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/#js-walking) from `yuku/analyzer` adds the semantic model to the context.

#### The context

One context object is reused across the whole walk, so do not store it.

```js
ctx.node;        // the current node
ctx.parent;      // its parent, or null at the walk root
ctx.key;         // the field on the parent holding this node
ctx.index;       // position in an array field, or null
ctx.ancestors(); // a copy of the ancestor chain, root first
```

#### Mutation

Handlers can mutate the AST in place.

| Operation                | Effect                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ctx.skip()`             | Do not descend into this node's children. `leave` still fires.                                                |
| `ctx.stop()`             | End the walk immediately.                                                                                     |
| `ctx.replace(node)`      | Swap the current node. The walk continues into the replacement's children and `leave` fires for its new type. |
| `ctx.remove()`           | Splice the node out of an array field, or null a plain field. Children are not walked, `leave` does not fire. |
| `ctx.insertBefore(node)` | Insert a sibling before the current node in an array field. The inserted node is not visited.                 |
| `ctx.insertAfter(node)`  | Insert a sibling after the current node in an array field. The walk visits it.                                |

A replacement with `start: 0, end: 0`, such as a [builder](#js-builders) node, takes the original node's span, so [source maps](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/#js-source-maps) still point at the original code.

```js
walk(program, {
  DebuggerStatement(node, ctx) {
    ctx.remove();
  },
});
```

#### findAll

`findAll` collects every node of the given types, in source order.

```js
import { findAll } from "yuku/ast";

findAll(program, "CallExpression");
findAll(program, ["ClassDeclaration", "TSInterfaceDeclaration"]);
```

`CHILD_KEYS` maps each node type to its child fields in traversal order, for walkers of your own.

### Builders

`b` has one typed constructor per node type. Spans default to 0, which `ctx.replace` fills from the replaced node.

```js
import { b } from "yuku/ast";

b.CallExpression({ callee: b.Identifier({ name: "f" }), arguments: [], optional: false });
```

### Guards

`is` has one guard per node type, per alias group, and for the shapes ESTree folds into one type: literal kinds, member expression kinds, and directives. Every guard accepts `null` and `undefined` and narrows.

```js
import { is } from "yuku/ast";

is.CallExpression(node);
is.Identifier(node, "require");
is.oneOf(node, ["FunctionDeclaration", "ClassDeclaration"]);
is.Expression(node);
is.StringLiteral(node);
is.StaticMemberExpression(node);
is.Directive(node);
```

### Imports and exports

`collectImports` and `collectExports` read a module's import and export declarations, one record per bound name, destructuring included.

```js
import { collectExports, collectImports } from "yuku/ast";

for (const record of collectImports(program)) {
  record.source;   // "./m"
  record.local;    // the local binding name
  record.imported; // "default", "*", or the export name
  record.typeOnly; // import type / import { type x }
  record.phase;    // "source" | "defer" | null
}

for (const record of collectExports(program)) {
  record.exported; // the exported name, null for a bare export *
  record.local;    // the backing local name, when there is one
  record.source;   // the re-export specifier, when there is one
  record.typeOnly;
}
```

`collectImportDeclaration` and `collectExportDeclaration` return the records of a single statement, for use inside a walk.

```js
walk(program, {
  ImportDeclaration(node) {
    records.push(...collectImportDeclaration(node));
  },
});
```

These read the syntax of one file. [`yuku/analyzer`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/#js-imports-and-exports) resolves them to bindings and links them across files.

### Utilities

```js
import {
  bindingIdentifiers, // every binding Identifier a pattern introduces
  isCallOf,           // isCallOf(node, "require")
  isWrapper,          // true for the wrappers unwrap strips
  literalValue,       // string | number | boolean | bigint | RegExp | null
  nameOf,             // Identifier name or string Literal value
  unwrap,             // strips parens and erased TypeScript assertion wrappers
} from "yuku/ast";
```

### Identifier names

```js
import { isIdentifierName, isValidIdentifier } from "yuku/ast";

isValidIdentifier("foo");   // true
isValidIdentifier("class"); // false, reserved
isIdentifierName("class");  // true, syntactically an IdentifierName
```

Plus `isIdentifierStart`, `isIdentifierChar`, `isKeyword`, `isReservedWord`, `isStrictReservedWord`, `isStrictBindReservedWord`, and `isStrictBindOnlyReservedWord`.

## Zig

The tree is flat. Nodes, child lists, and strings live in arrays in one arena, and `tree.deinit()` frees them all at once. Four types refer into it.

| Type         | Is                                                                           |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NodeIndex`  | A node's position in `nodes`, `.null` for an absent child                    |
| `IndexRange` | A child list, a start and length in `extras`                                 |
| `String`     | Text, a zero-copy slice of the source or an entry in the pool                |
| `Span`       | A source range in bytes                                                      |

## Reading the tree

`tree.root` is the `program` node, and four calls read everything below it.

```zig
tree.data(idx)    // a node's payload, a tagged union
tree.span(idx)    // its source range
tree.extra(range) // a list of child nodes
tree.string(text) // the bytes of a string
```

Tags are snake_case, and [ast.zig](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/src/parser/ast.zig) defines every one with its fields.

```zig
switch (tree.data(idx)) {
    .variable_declaration => |decl| {
        for (tree.extra(decl.declarators)) |declarator| {
            _ = declarator;
        }
    },
    .identifier_reference => |id| {
        std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{tree.string(id.name)});
    },
    else => {},
}
```

Predicates classify a payload in one call: `isExpression`, `isStatement`, `isDeclaration`, `isLiteral`, `isPattern`, `isCallable`, `isIteration`, and `isTypeContext`. To walk the whole tree, use the [traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/).

`tree.source`, `tree.lang`, and `tree.source_type` hold what was parsed, and `isTs()`, `isJsx()`, and `isModule()` ask about them.

## Building and editing

Every change goes through the tree and lands in its arena.

```zig
const name = try tree.addString("total");          // interned, deduplicated
const id = try tree.addNode(.{ .identifier_reference = .{ .name = name } }, span);
const list = try tree.addExtra(&.{id});            // a child list
tree.setData(idx, data);                           // replace a payload
tree.setSpan(idx, span);
tree.setIdentifierName(idx, name);                 // any identifier kind
const text = tree.sourceSlice(start, end);         // a String over the source, no copy
try tree.addDiagnostic(.{ .message = "unused", .span = span });
```

`ast.Tree.initEmpty(allocator)` starts a tree with no source. The [transform](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#transform) traverser makes these changes during a walk.

## Comments

The `comments` option collects every comment into `tree.comments`, attaches each to its node, or both. An attached comment records whether it sits `before`, `after`, or `inside` its node, so it moves with its node through transforms and [codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/) prints it in place.

```zig
for (tree.commentsOf(idx)) |c| {
    std.debug.print("{t} {s}\n", .{ c.position, tree.string(c.value) });
}
```

## Tokens

`.tokens = true` keeps every token in `tree.tokens`, as the parser resolved it.

```zig
for (tree.tokens) |token| {
    std.debug.print("{t} {s}\n", .{ token.tag, token.text(tree.source) });
}
```

```zig
token.tag.isKeyword()             // also isReserved, isIdentifierLike, isNumericLiteral,
                                  // and the operator kinds
token.tag.precedence()            // operator precedence, 0 when none
token.hasLineTerminatorBefore()   // what ASI reads
token.isEscaped()                 // also hasInvalidEscape and hasLoneSurrogates
```

The list ends with an `eof` token. Every node other than `program`, `template_element`, and `jsx_empty_expression` starts and ends on a token boundary, so its tokens are a contiguous run.

# Semantic Analysis

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/

Semantic analysis builds a model of a program: its scopes, symbols, and references, with each reference resolved to the binding it names. It also reports the early errors that need scopes, such as redeclarations and private fields used outside their class.

## JavaScript

```js
import { analyze } from "yuku/analyzer";

const module = analyze(`const double = (n: number) => n * 2; double(21);`, { path: "math.ts" });

module.rootScope.find("double").references.length; // 1
```

An `Analyzer` is a project, which links imports across its files.

```js
import { Analyzer } from "yuku/analyzer";

const project = new Analyzer();

project.setFile("a.ts", `export const value = 1;`);
project.setFile("b.ts", `export { value as renamed } from "./a.ts";`);
project.setFile("c.ts", `import { renamed } from "./b.ts"; renamed;`);

project.module("c.ts").rootScope.find("renamed").definition().binding.name; // "value"
```

### Analyzer

```js
const project = new Analyzer({
  // a path in the project, false for a module outside it, null when it cannot be resolved
  resolve: (specifier, importer) => aliases.get(specifier) ?? null,
});

project.setFile(path, source, options); // Module, replacing any at the same path
project.deleteFile(path);               // whether it was in the project
project.module(path);                   // Module | undefined
project.modules;                        // ReadonlyMap<string, Module>
project.diagnostics;                    // every module's diagnostics, and the failed links
project.link();                         // links now, cross-file queries link on demand otherwise
```

`setFile` takes a string or UTF-8 bytes, and the `lang`, `sourceType`, `preserveParens`, `attachComments`, and `tokens` options of the [parser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/#js-options). `analyze(source, options)` is a project of one file, and also takes `path`. Both `new Analyzer` and `analyze` take a custom build as `wasm`, such as one with a [dialect](https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/#javascript).

The default resolver matches relative specifiers to files in the project, probing extensions and index files as TypeScript does, so `./a.js` finds `a.ts`. A package or an asset such as `./app.css` is external, and a relative specifier with no match is reported as a warning.

Diagnostics have the [shape of the parser's](https://yuku.fyi/parser/#js-diagnostics), with the `path` of their module.

### Module

```js
module.analyzer;    // the Analyzer it belongs to
module.path;
module.source;
module.ast;         // the ESTree / TypeScript-ESTree Program
module.comments;
module.tokens;      // with tokens: true
module.diagnostics;
module.isCurrent;   // false once its path is set again or deleted

module.scopes;               // Scope[], by id
module.rootScope;            // the module scope, or the global scope of a script
module.bindings;             // Binding[], by id
module.references;           // Reference[], in source order
module.unresolvedReferences; // globals and undeclared names
module.imports;              // Import[]
module.exports;              // Export[]
module.moduleFlags;          // { usesRequire, usesModule, usesExports, usesImportMeta }
module.dependencies;         // the modules it imports from
module.dependents;           // the modules that import it

module.bindingOf(node);      // the binding a node declares or refers to
module.referenceOf(node);
module.scopeOf(node);
module.parentOf(node);
module.ancestors(node);      // the node, then each parent up to the root
module.nodeAt(offset);       // the innermost node at a UTF-16 offset
module.lookup("x", { from: scope, space: "value" }); // resolves a name as code there would
module.capturesOf(fn);       // [{ binding, references, isWritten }], the outer bindings it uses
module.exportedNames();      // through export * and module augmentations
module.resolveExport("x");   // { module, binding, augmentations }, the binding behind an export
module.walk(visitors, root);
module.walkAsync(visitors, root);
module.findAll(types);       // every node of the given types, in source order
```

A node is the same object in `module.ast` and in every result, so each query takes the node you hold. The model describes the source as analyzed, and does not follow later edits to the AST.

### Scope

```js
scope.id;
scope.module;
scope.kind;        // "global" | "module" | "function" | "functionBody" | "block" | "class"
                   // | "staticBlock" | "expressionName" | "tsModule"
scope.strict;
scope.node;        // the node that creates it
scope.parent;
scope.hoistTarget; // where a var declared in it lands
scope.bindings;

scope.find("x");       // a binding it declares
scope.contains(other); // other is this scope or inside it
scope.ancestors();     // this scope, then each parent
```

### Binding

```js
binding.id;
binding.module;
binding.name;
binding.scope;
binding.declarations; // each declaration's name node, overloads and merges included
binding.references;   // its uses in this module
binding.flags;        // a BindingFlags bitset

binding.has(BindingFlags.Function);
binding.hasAll(BindingFlags.Const | BindingFlags.Exported);
binding.visibleIn("type");

binding.definition();     // { module, binding, augmentations } it imports, followed across modules
binding.findReferences(); // its uses across the project
```

A `definition` with a null `binding` is a whole module namespace, as `import * as ns` binds. Its `augmentations` are the bindings of `declare module "m"` blocks in other modules that merge into it.

### Reference

```js
reference.id;
reference.module;
reference.name;
reference.scope;
reference.node;           // the Identifier or JSXIdentifier
reference.binding;        // null for a global or undeclared name
reference.space;          // "value" | "type" | "namespace" | "typeof" | "any"
reference.inTypePosition; // erased with the types
reference.isWrite;        // x = 1, x++, for (x of xs)
```

Names resolve per space, as [Declaration spaces](#declaration-spaces) describes.

### Imports and exports

```js
imp.id;
imp.module;
imp.kind;           // "named" | "namespace" | "sideEffect" | "importEquals" | "dynamic" | "require" | "augmentation"
imp.name;           // the imported name, "default" for a default import
imp.local;          // the binding it declares
imp.isNamespace;    // it binds a whole module, as namespace and importEquals do
imp.specifier;
imp.typeOnly;
imp.phase;          // "source" | "defer" | null
imp.node;
imp.resolvedModule;

exp.id;
exp.module;
exp.kind;           // "named" | "reExport" | "namespace" | "star" | "equals" | "global"
exp.name;           // the exported name, null for star, equals, and global
exp.globalName;     // the N of export as namespace N
exp.local;          // the binding it exports
exp.specifier;      // the module it re-exports from
exp.fromName;       // the name a reExport takes from it
exp.typeOnly;
exp.node;
exp.resolvedModule;
```

They are the [module records](#module-records), linked. Linking follows the specification's ResolveExport, so `export *` never forwards `default`, and a name two stars provide differently is reported as ambiguous.

### Walking

`module.walk` is the [walker of `yuku/ast`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#js-walking), with the model in its context.

```js
module.walk({
  CallExpression(node, ctx) {
    ctx.binding;   // module.bindingOf(node)
    ctx.reference; // module.referenceOf(node)
    ctx.scope;     // module.scopeOf(node)
    ctx.module;
  },
});
```

### BindingFlags

The [symbol flags](#symbols), as `binding.flags` holds them.

| Flag                     | Set on                                  |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `FunctionScopedVariable` | `var`, a parameter, or a catch variable |
| `BlockScopedVariable`    | `let`, `const`, `using`, `await using`  |
| `Function`               | a function                              |
| `Class`                  | a class                                 |
| `RegularEnum`            | `enum`                                  |
| `ConstEnum`              | `const enum`                            |
| `ValueModule`            | a namespace with runtime content        |
| `Interface`              | `interface`                             |
| `TypeAlias`              | `type`                                  |
| `TypeParameter`          | `<T>`, `infer T`, a mapped type key     |
| `NamespaceModule`        | a namespace of any kind                 |
| `ValueImport`            | `import x`, `import { x }`              |
| `TypeImport`             | `import type`, `import { type x }`      |
| `Const`                  | `const`, `using`, `await using`         |
| `Ambient`                | `declare`                               |
| `Parameter`              | a parameter                             |
| `CatchVariable`          | `catch (e)`                             |
| `Exported`               | `export`, or implicitly in ambient code |
| `Default`                | `export default <declaration>`          |
| `EnumMember`             | an enum member                          |
| `Variable`               | any variable                            |
| `Import`                 | any import                              |
| `ValueSpace`             | anything visible at runtime             |
| `TypeSpace`              | anything usable as a type               |
| `NamespaceSpace`         | what a dotted type name can start from  |

## Zig

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, source, .{});
defer tree.deinit();

const semantic = try parser.semantic.analyze(&tree);
```

`analyze` returns the `Semantic` model and appends its errors to `tree.diagnostics`. The model lives in the tree's arena and describes the tree as parsed, so analyze again after a transform. To run your own hooks during the analysis walk, use the [semantic traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#semantic).

When only the errors matter, `check` reports the same ones faster, without building the model.

```zig
try parser.semantic.check(&tree);
```

## The model

- A **scope** is a lexical environment, with its kind, its parent, its strictness, and the scope its `var`s hoist to.
- A **symbol** is a declared binding, with its flags and every declaration.
- A **reference** is a use of a name, resolved to its symbol, or to `.none` for a global or undeclared name. It records whether it writes, as assignments, `++`, and `for-of` targets do. JSX component tags and type-predicate parameters are references too, so a rename sees every site.

Every node leads into the model, and every symbol leads back to its nodes.

```zig
semantic.symbolOf(node)             // the symbol a node declares or refers to, or null
semantic.referenceOf(node)          // the reference at an identifier, or null
semantic.scopeOf(node)              // the innermost scope around a node
semantic.parentOf(node)             // its parent, or null at the root
semantic.ancestors(node)            // the node, then each parent up to the root

semantic.symbol(id)                 // and scope(id), reference(id)
semantic.decls(symbol)              // each declaration's name node
semantic.uses(symbol)               // each reference to it

semantic.bindings(scope)            // the symbols a scope declares
semantic.binding(scope, "x")        // one of them by name
semantic.lookup(scope, "x", .value) // name resolution from any scope

semantic.iterSymbols()              // and iterScopes, iterReferences
```

`Symbol`, `Scope`, and `Reference` are in `parser.traverser.semantic`. A declaration's name node is an identifier, or a string literal for a quoted enum member. Ids are dense and ordered, symbols by first declaration and references by source position, so "first declaration" and "earliest use" are index comparisons.

Renaming a binding everywhere is two loops.

```zig
const name = try tree.addString("renamed");
for (semantic.decls(symbol)) |node| tree.setIdentifierName(node, name);
for (semantic.uses(symbol)) |ref| tree.setIdentifierName(semantic.reference(ref).node, name);
```

Unused bindings and undeclared names are one loop each.

```zig
var symbols = semantic.iterSymbols();
while (symbols.next()) |entry| {
    if (semantic.uses(entry.id).len == 0) std.debug.print("unused {s}\n", .{tree.string(entry.symbol.name)});
}

var references = semantic.iterReferences();
while (references.next()) |entry| {
    if (entry.reference.symbol == .none) std.debug.print("undeclared {s}\n", .{tree.string(entry.reference.name)});
}
```

## Scopes

The scope tree follows the specification.

- A catch clause shares its scope with its body, unless its parameter has a default value or a computed key.
- A named function or class expression has a scope of its own for its name.
- A function body scopes its `let` and `const` apart from the parameters, as TypeScript does.
- A class decorator sees the scope around its class, and a member decorator sees the class scope.
- Strict mode comes from modules, classes, and `"use strict"` directives.

## Symbols

A symbol's `flags` record its declaration kinds, such as `function_scoped_var`, `block_scoped_var`, `function`, `class`, `interface`, `regular_enum`, and `import`, and its modifiers, such as `const_var`, `exported`, and `ambient`. Masks test a category in one call, as `flags.intersects(Symbol.value_space)` does, with `variable`, `any_import`, `value_space`, `type_space`, and `namespace_space`. `flags.visibleIn(space)` tells whether a reference in a space can bind to it.

One rule decides both merging and redeclaration. Each declaration kind has an exclusion mask in `Symbol.Excludes`. A new declaration conflicts with an existing symbol whose flags intersect it, and merges into that symbol otherwise. Function overloads, a `class` and an `interface`, and a `namespace` and an `enum` all merge this way. A namespace or enum declared in several blocks merges too, and each block sees the exports or members of the others.

## Declaration spaces

Resolution follows TypeScript. A name resolves in one space, and a binding outside that space does not shadow it.

```ts
type T = string;
function f() {
  const T = 1;
  let x: T; // the outer `type T`, as in tsc
  T;        // the inner `const T`
}
```

A reference resolves in `.value` for runtime uses, `.type` for annotations, `.namespace` for the head of a dotted name such as `ns.T` or `import x = ns.T`, `.typeof` for value uses inside a type, or `.any` for alias positions such as `export { x }`. A class and an enum live in both the value and type spaces, and every reference carries its space, so a rename can change a value without touching a same-named type.

## Module records

`module_record.collect` lists a module's imports and exports, modeled on the specification's ImportEntry and ExportEntry records, each with the local symbol behind it.

```zig
const records = try parser.semantic.module_record.collect(&tree, &semantic);
// records.imports, records.exports, records.flags
```

An import has a `kind`, `name`, `symbol`, `specifier`, `type_only`, `phase`, `node`, and `scope`. Its kind is `named`, `namespace`, `side_effect`, `import_equals`, `dynamic`, `require`, or `augmentation`. Dynamic `import()` and `require()` calls count when their specifier is a string literal. An `augmentation` is a `declare module "m"` block in a module, which merges the declarations of its body `scope` into the exports of `m`.

An export has a `kind`, `name`, `symbol`, `from_name`, `specifier`, `type_only`, and `node`, and its kind is `named`, `re_export`, `namespace`, `star`, `equals`, or `global`. As in TypeScript, a declaration file that is a module but has no export statement exports every declaration but its imports.

CommonJS exports have no static shape, so `records.flags` records whether the file uses `require`, `module`, `exports`, or `import.meta`.

# Traverse

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/

The traverser walks a tree and calls your visitor's hooks at every node. Pick the mode for what your tool needs to know as it walks.

| Mode                      | Tracks                          | Returns                                   | For                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| [`basic`](#visitors)      | the path from the root          | nothing                                   | pattern matching, counters, simple lints    |
| [`scoped`](#scoped)       | the path and lexical scopes     | a `ScopeTree`                             | checks that depend on scope or strict mode  |
| [`semantic`](#semantic)   | scopes, symbols, and references | the [`Semantic`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) model | analysis that needs to know what names mean |
| [`transform`](#transform) | the path, with a mutable tree   | nothing                                   | rewrites, codemods, and desugaring          |

In `basic`, `scoped`, and `semantic`, `ctx.tree` is a `*const Tree`, so a visitor cannot mutate what it reads. Only `transform` hands it a mutable tree.

In JavaScript, [`walk`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#js-walking) from `yuku/ast` walks any ESTree AST, and [`module.walk`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/#js-walking) from `yuku/analyzer` adds the semantic model to the walk.

## Visitors

A visitor is a struct with `enter_<tag>` and `exit_<tag>` methods, named after node tags. Each hook receives its node's payload already unpacked. This one counts functions in `basic` mode.

```zig
const std = @import("std");
const parser = @import("parser");
const ast = parser.ast;
const traverser = parser.traverser;
const basic = traverser.basic;

const Counter = struct {
    functions: u32 = 0,

    pub fn enter_function(
        self: *Counter,
        _: ast.Function,
        _: ast.NodeIndex,
        _: *basic.Ctx,
    ) traverser.Action {
        self.functions += 1;
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var counter = Counter{};
try basic.traverse(Counter, &tree, &counter);
std.debug.print("{d} functions\n", .{counter.functions});
```

A misspelled hook or a wrong payload type is a compile error. `enter_node` and `exit_node` fire for every node, with the `ast.NodeData` payload. The walk is depth-first with siblings in source order.

An enter hook returns a `traverser.Action`: `.proceed` to walk into the children, `.skip` to pass over them, or `.stop` to end the walk. It may return it in an error union to `try` an allocation. An exit hook returns nothing.

Every mode's context has `ctx.tree` and `ctx.path`. The path knows the current node's `parent()`, its `ancestor(n)` with the current node at 0, its `ancestors()` from the current node up, and its `depth()`.

## Scoped

`ctx.scope` follows the walk into and out of every scope, with `currentScope()`, `hoistTarget()`, and `isStrict()`. This lint finds each `var` that escapes the block it is written in.

```zig
const scoped = traverser.scoped;

const VarInBlock = struct {
    found: u32 = 0,

    pub fn enter_variable_declaration(
        self: *VarInBlock,
        decl: ast.VariableDeclaration,
        _: ast.NodeIndex,
        ctx: *scoped.Ctx,
    ) traverser.Action {
        if (decl.kind == .@"var" and ctx.scope.currentScope().kind == .block) self.found += 1;
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var lint = VarInBlock{};
const scopes = try scoped.traverse(VarInBlock, &tree, &lint);
```

On `{ var b; } for (var i = 0;;) {}` it finds `b` and `i`. The walk also returns every scope it saw as a `ScopeTree`, and an empty visitor returns just that.

## Semantic

The walk builds the [`Semantic`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) model as it goes and returns it. During the walk, `ctx.inTypePosition()` and `ctx.inTsNamespace()` tell where it is, and `ctx.symbols.binding(scope, name)` finds a name declared so far. References resolve when the walk ends, so a visitor collects nodes and queries the model after. This one finds the types a file imports.

```zig
const sem = traverser.semantic;

const TypeNames = struct {
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    nodes: std.ArrayList(ast.NodeIndex) = .empty,

    pub fn enter_identifier_reference(
        self: *TypeNames,
        _: ast.IdentifierReference,
        index: ast.NodeIndex,
        ctx: *sem.Ctx,
    ) std.mem.Allocator.Error!traverser.Action {
        if (ctx.inTypePosition()) try self.nodes.append(self.allocator, index);
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var names = TypeNames{ .allocator = tree.allocator() };
const semantic = try sem.traverse(TypeNames, &tree, &names);

for (names.nodes.items) |node| {
    const id = semantic.symbolOf(node) orelse continue; // a global type
    const symbol = semantic.symbol(id);
    if (symbol.flags.intersects(sem.Symbol.any_import)) {
        std.debug.print("imported type {s}\n", .{tree.string(symbol.name)});
    }
}
```

On `import type { User } from "./user"; type Id = string; let user: User, id: Id;` it prints `User`. `semantic.analyze` is this mode with a visitor that reports the early errors.

## Transform

A `transform` hook rewrites the tree in place. The walker re-reads a node after its enter hook, so it walks the replacement. This one turns `total = price + tax` into `total = price * tax`.

```zig
const transform = traverser.transform;

const AddToMultiply = struct {
    pub fn enter_binary_expression(
        _: *AddToMultiply,
        expr: ast.BinaryExpression,
        index: ast.NodeIndex,
        ctx: *transform.Ctx,
    ) traverser.Action {
        if (expr.operator == .add) {
            ctx.tree.setData(index, .{ .binary_expression = .{
                .left = expr.left,
                .right = expr.right,
                .operator = .multiply,
            } });
        }
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var rewrite = AddToMultiply{};
try transform.traverse(AddToMultiply, &tree, &rewrite);
```

The tree's [building and editing](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#building-and-editing) calls, such as `addNode`, `addString`, and `setIdentifierName`, work during the walk. After wrapping a node in a new parent, return `.skip`, so the walker does not enter the moved node again. [Codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/) prints the result.

To build a separate output tree, start one with `ast.Tree.initEmpty` and walk the input tree in any mode. Modes compose as passes, such as a transform followed by a semantic walk over its result.

## Your own mode

Each mode is a context type over one walker. A context of your own has a `tree` field and `enter(index, data)` and `exit(index, data)` methods, and `traverser.Layer` runs them around your visitor's hooks.

```zig
var layer = traverser.Layer(MyCtx, V){ .inner = &visitor };
try traverser.walk(MyCtx, traverser.Layer(MyCtx, V), &layer, &ctx);
```

[basic.zig](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/src/parser/traverser/basic.zig) is the smallest mode, a context that tracks the path.

# Codegen

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/

The codegen prints a tree back to source, with optional type stripping, minification, and source maps.

## JavaScript

```js
import { parse } from "yuku";
import { generate } from "yuku/codegen";

const { code, map, diagnostics } = generate(parse("const x = 1 + 2;").program);
// code is "const x = 1 + 2;"
```

`yuku/codegen` prints an ESTree AST from any parser, with the [same output](https://yuku.fyi/testing/#codegen) as the Zig codegen.

### Result

`generate` takes a `Program` or any single node, such as an object property, and returns a `GenerateResult`.

```ts
interface GenerateResult {
  code: string;
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[]; // empty on a clean run
  map: SourceMap | null;     // with sourceMap
}
```

`diagnostics` has the [shape of the parser's](https://yuku.fyi/parser/#js-diagnostics).

### Options

```js
generate(program, { strip: true, minify: true, sourceMap: { source } });
```

| Option      | Type                                                        | Default      | Description                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `strip`     | `boolean`                                                   | `false`      | Drop TypeScript-only syntax, see [Type stripping](#type-stripping).                           |
| `minify`    | `boolean \| MinifyOptions`                                  | `false`      | Minify the output, see [Minification](#js-minification).                                      |
| `format`    | `"pretty" \| "compact"`                                     | `"pretty"`   | `"compact"` emits only the separators the grammar requires.                                   |
| `indent`    | `number`                                                    | `2`          | Spaces per level in pretty format, from 0 to 255.                                             |
| `quotes`    | `"preserve" \| "double" \| "single" \| "shortest"`          | `"preserve"` | Quote style for string literals, see [Quotes](#js-quotes).                                    |
| `comments`  | `boolean \| "all" \| "some" \| "none" \| "line" \| "block"` | `"some"`     | Which attached comments to print, see [Comments](#js-comments).                               |
| `sourceMap` | `SourceMapOptions`                                          | none         | Emit a Source Map V3, see [Source maps](#js-source-maps).                                     |
| `print`     | `Printers`                                                  | none         | Print node types the printer does not know, see [Printing new nodes](#js-printing-new-nodes). |

An invalid value throws a `TypeError`, or a `RangeError` for `indent`.

### Minification

`minify: true` enables every switch, and an object picks them. Enabled switches override `format` and `quotes`.

| Switch       | Behavior                                                  |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `whitespace` | Emit compact whitespace.                                  |
| `syntax`     | Apply the size-reducing [syntax rewrites](#minification). |
| `quotes`     | Use whichever quote needs fewer escapes per literal.      |

```js
generate(program, { minify: { syntax: true } }); // rewrites only, readable output
```

### Quotes

| Value        | Behavior                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"preserve"` | Keep each literal's source quote style, re-escaping the content.       |
| `"double"`   | Force double quotes.                                                   |
| `"single"`   | Force single quotes.                                                   |
| `"shortest"` | Pick whichever quote needs fewer escapes per literal, double on a tie. |

### Comments

Comments print from the nodes they are attached to, so parse with [`attachComments: true`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/#js-comments) to keep them.

| Value               | Behavior                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"some"`            | Legal headers, JSDoc, and `@`/`#` annotations, the bundler convention. The default. |
| `"all"` or `true`   | Every comment.                                                                      |
| `"none"` or `false` | No comments.                                                                        |
| `"line"`            | `// ...` only.                                                                      |
| `"block"`           | `/* ... */` only.                                                                   |

```js
const { program } = parse(`// hello\nconst x = 1;`, { attachComments: true });
generate(program, { comments: true }).code;
// "// hello\nconst x = 1;"
```

### Source maps

Pass the original source to emit a Source Map V3 alongside the code.

```js
const { code, map } = generate(program, {
  sourceMap: { source, file: "out.js", sourceFileName: "in.js", sourcesContent: source },
});

const output = `${code}\n//# sourceMappingURL=out.js.map`;
const mapJson = JSON.stringify(map);
```

| Field            | Description                                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `source`         | **Required.** The original source text.         |
| `file`           | Output filename, embedded as `file`.            |
| `sourceFileName` | Source filename, the single entry of `sources`. |
| `sourceRoot`     | Embedded as `sourceRoot`.                       |
| `sourcesContent` | The single entry of `sourcesContent`.           |

`map` is a Source Map V3 object, ready for `JSON.stringify`, with columns in UTF-16 code units as in [Source maps](#source-maps).

```ts
interface SourceMap {
  version: 3;
  file: string | null;
  sourceRoot: string | null;
  sources: string[];
  sourcesContent: (string | null)[] | null;
  names: string[];
  mappings: string;
}
```

### Printing new nodes

`print` prints node types the printer does not know, such as the nodes of a [dialect](https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/#javascript), keyed by `type`. Each function drives the printer, which prints the standard nodes inside with their comments and formatting.

```js
generate(program, {
  print: {
    PipelineExpression(node, p) {
      p.node(node.left);
      p.write(" |> ");
      p.node(node.right);
    },
  },
});
```

| Call           | Behavior                                            |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `write(code)`  | Write code, spaced from what precedes it if needed. |
| `space()`      | Write a space in the pretty format.                 |
| `node(node)`   | Print any node, with its comments.                  |
| `block(items)` | Print a list of statements between braces.          |

A type the printer knows always prints as standard, and a type with no printer throws.

## Zig

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, "const x: number = 1;", .{ .lang = .ts });
defer tree.deinit();

const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{ .strip = true });
defer result.deinit(allocator);

std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{result.code}); // const x = 1;
```

`generate` leaves the tree unchanged and returns the `code`, its `diagnostics` as `ast.Diagnostic`, and the source `map`, owned by the allocator it was given and freed with `result.deinit`. It fails only with `error.OutOfMemory`.

## Options

| Field        | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `strip`      | `false`     | Drop TypeScript-only syntax, see [Type stripping](#type-stripping)                                                                                  |
| `minify`     | `false`     | Size-reducing syntax rewrites, see [Minification](#minification)                                                                                    |
| `format`     | `.pretty`   | `.compact` emits only the whitespace the grammar requires                                                                                           |
| `indent`     | `2`         | Spaces per level                                                                                                                                    |
| `quotes`     | `.preserve` | `.preserve`, `.double`, `.single`, or `.shortest`                                                                                                   |
| `comments`   | `.some`     | Which [attached comments](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#comments) to print, `.some` for legal headers, JSDoc, and annotations, or `.all`, `.none`, `.line`, `.block` |
| `source_map` | `null`      | Emit a Source Map V3, see [Source maps](#source-maps)                                                                                               |

Comments print from the nodes they are attached to, so parse with `.comments = .attached` or `.both` to keep them.

## Type stripping

`strip` prints TypeScript as JavaScript. Types, interfaces, type aliases, generics, assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`, `declare`, and `abstract` strip cleanly.

Constructs that emit runtime code, such as `enum`, `namespace`, `module`, `export =`, `import = require()`, and parameter properties, are left out and reported in `diagnostics`, since converting them is transpilation, not stripping. A parameter property keeps its plain parameter, and the rest of the file still prints. Their ambient forms, such as `declare enum` and `import type X = require(...)`, have no runtime code and strip silently.

## Minification

`minify` rewrites the syntax, and combined with `.compact` and `.shortest` it fully minifies.

```zig
const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{
    .minify = true,
    .format = .compact,
    .quotes = .shortest,
});
// const enabled = true; const size = 1000000;
// prints as const enabled=!0;const size=1e6
```

- `true` and `false` become `!0` and `!1`.
- Numbers take their shortest form, so `1000000` becomes `1e6` and `0.5` becomes `.5`.
- `obj["foo"]` becomes `obj.foo` when the key is a valid identifier, and `{ "foo": x }` becomes `{ foo: x }` when safe.
- `</script`, `<!--`, and `-->` are escaped in strings and untagged templates, so the output is safe inside a `<script>` tag. Tagged templates keep their raw text, since the tag reads it.

## Source maps

```zig
const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{
    .source_map = .{
        .source = source,           // required for a map
        .file = "out.js",
        .source_file_name = "in.js",
        .source_root = null,
        .sources_content = source,
    },
});
defer result.deinit(allocator);

const map = result.map.?; // version, file, source_root, sources, sources_content, names, mappings
```

Columns are in UTF-16 code units, as browser devtools and source map libraries expect.

A build that never needs maps can compile them out, for a smaller binary. `map` is then always `null`.

```zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{ .@"codegen-source-maps" = false });
```

# Dialects

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/dialect/

A dialect adds syntax to the languages Yuku parses, such as a language proposal, a template syntax, or a language of your own on JavaScript. It is one Zig file compiled into the parser. The file claims input at a few positions in the grammar, parses there with Yuku's own grammar, and builds nodes of kinds it declares. The rest of Yuku works on those nodes.

## When to use one

Use a dialect when your syntax lives inside JavaScript: in expressions, statements, or JSX, mixed with code that must parse, analyze, and print as it always does. Sugar over JavaScript is a dialect too, parsed into nodes of its own and lowered to standard ones by a [transform](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#transform) pass.

A format that only embeds JavaScript in a structure of its own, such as markup with script blocks, needs no dialect. Parse its structure yourself and call `parser.parse` on each embedded block.

## An example

This dialect adds the `|>` pipeline operator, with `%` as the value piped in.

```zig
// pipeline.zig
const std = @import("std");
const yuku = @import("parser");

const ast = yuku.ast;
const dialect = yuku.dialect;

pub const files: []const dialect.File = &.{.{ .extension = ".js", .lang = .js }};

pub const Node = enum {
    pipeline,
    topic,

    pub fn shape(node: Node) dialect.Shape {
        return switch (node) {
            .pipeline => .{ .type = "PipelineExpression", .fields = &.{ "left", "right" } },
            .topic => .{ .type = "TopicReference" },
        };
    }
};

pub fn operator(
    p: *dialect.Parser,
    left: ast.NodeIndex,
    precedence: u8,
) dialect.Error!dialect.Claim {
    if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, p.source()[p.token().span.start..], "|>")) return .decline;
    if (precedence > ast.Precedence.Assignment) return .end;

    if (!try p.advance() or !try p.advance()) return .failed;
    const right = try p.parseExpression(ast.Precedence.Assignment + 1) orelse return .failed;
    const span: ast.Span = .{ .start = p.tree().span(left).start, .end = p.tree().span(right).end };
    return .{ .node = try p.addNode(.pipeline, &.{ left, right }, span) };
}

pub fn expression(p: *dialect.Parser) dialect.Error!dialect.Claim {
    const token = p.token();
    if (token.tag != .percent) return .decline;

    if (!try p.advance()) return .failed;
    return .{ .node = try p.addNode(.topic, &.{}, token.span) };
}

pub fn print(w: *dialect.Printer, kind: Node, children: []const ast.NodeIndex) dialect.Error!void {
    switch (kind) {
        .pipeline => {
            try w.node(children[0]);
            try w.write(" |> ");
            try w.node(children[1]);
        },
        .topic => try w.write("%"),
    }
}
```

Compiled in, it parses `const total = prices |> sum(%) |> round(%, 2);` with the pipelines grouping left to right. The calls inside them resolve and walk like any others, codegen prints the line back as written, and in JavaScript each pipeline decodes as `{ type: "PipelineExpression", left, right }`.

## Compiling one in

```zig
// build.zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
    .dialect = b.path("src/pipeline.zig"),
});
my_module.addImport("parser", yuku.module("parser"));
```

Inside the Yuku repository, `zig build -Ddialect=src/pipeline.zig` does the same. The dialect imports the parser it is compiled into as `@import("parser")`, so its functions take that parser's own types. A binary holds one parser, and so one dialect.

Every dialect declares `files`, the extensions of the files your syntax lives in, each with the standard language it extends. [In JavaScript](#javascript), they decide which files parse with the dialect. In Zig, a parse opts in with `dialect`, so one parser reads both your syntax and standard files.

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, source, .{ .dialect = true });
```

## Positions

A dialect claims input with a `pub fn` named after a position, the start of a production in the standard grammar. The parser asks the dialect there before parsing the production, and parses standard syntax when the dialect declines.

| Position           | Asked at                                                     | Also receives               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `statement`        | the start of every statement                                 |                             |
| `expression`       | the start of every operand, before any prefix operator       |                             |
| `operator`         | after an operand, where an infix or postfix operator follows | the operand, the precedence |
| `function_body`    | where a function, method, or arrow function body begins      |                             |
| `jsx_child`        | the start of each JSX child                                  | its byte offset, the parent |
| `jsx_attribute`    | a `{` that opens a JSX attribute                             |                             |
| `jsx_element_name` | the start of an element name, in an opening or closing tag   |                             |
| `module_specifier` | a module specifier that is not a string                      |                             |

```zig
pub fn statement(p: *dialect.Parser) dialect.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn operator(p: *dialect.Parser, left: ast.NodeIndex, precedence: u8) dialect.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn jsx_child(p: *dialect.Parser, offset: u32, parent: ast.NodeIndex) dialect.Error!dialect.Claim
```

Each answers with a `Claim`.

| Claim      | Means                                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.decline` | not the dialect's syntax, with nothing consumed                  |
| `.node`    | the node it parsed, with the current token past it               |
| `.failed`  | it reported a diagnostic                                         |
| `.end`     | at `operator` only, the expression ends before the current token |

- `operator` receives the lowest [precedence](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#tokens) that continues the expression. A dialect operator that binds more loosely answers `.end`, so an enclosing expression takes it, as the example does.
- A JSX child ends on its last token, which stays current, since the parser reads the text after it by offset. `parent` is the opening element or fragment.
- Positions apply inside every production a dialect parses, so its syntax nests in standard syntax and standard syntax in its own.
- A position should decline anything the standard grammar accepts, unless the dialect means to read that input differently.
- A function that takes a `*dialect.Parser` without naming a position is a compile error, so a misspelled position never compiles to one that never runs.

## The parser

`dialect.Parser` is the parser as a dialect drives it.

| Call                                           | Does                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `token()`, `advance()`, `expect(tag, message)` | read and consume tokens                                                                  |
| `tokenAt(offset)`                              | the token at or after a byte offset, read without moving the parser, for lookahead       |
| `source()`                                     | the source text                                                                          |
| `seek(offset)`                                 | make the token at a byte offset current, in a JSX child                                  |
| `checkpoint()`, `rewind(checkpoint)`           | try a parse and undo it                                                                  |
| `semicolon(end)`                               | end a statement, with automatic semicolon insertion                                      |
| `report(span, message)`                        | report a diagnostic                                                                      |
| `parseStatement()`                             | parse a statement                                                                        |
| `parseExpression(precedence)`                  | parse an expression whose operators bind at `precedence` or tighter                      |
| `parseBindingPattern()`                        | parse an identifier, array, or object pattern, with its type annotation in TypeScript    |
| `parseJsxExpressionContainer()`                | parse the `{ expression }` at a `{` inside a tag                                         |
| `parseJsxElement()`                            | parse the element or fragment at a `<`, leaving its last `>` current                     |
| `addNode(kind, children, span)`, `list()`      | build the dialect's nodes                                                                |
| `addJsxText(span)`                             | add JSX text, its character references decoded                                           |
| `addComment(type, span)`                       | record a comment the dialect reads where the standard grammar reads none, as in text     |
| `tree()`                                       | build standard nodes with the tree's [building calls](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#building-and-editing) |

`list()` collects children of unknown number on the parser's scratch space.

```zig
var children = p.list();
defer children.reset();
while (p.token().tag != .right_brace) {
    try children.append(try p.parseStatement() orelse return .failed);
}
const node = try p.addNode(.block, children.items(), span);
```

## Node shapes

A dialect lists its node kinds in a `Node` enum. Each of its nodes is an `ast.Dialect`, its `kind` of that enum and its `children` in source order, `.null` for an absent part. `shape` says what each kind is.

| Field              | Means                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`             | the `type` the node decodes to in JavaScript                                            |
| `fields`           | the names of its children, in order. A name ending in `[]` takes the children left over |
| `block_scope`      | the node opens a block scope                                                            |
| `lexical_bindings` | a binding identifier inside it declares a `let`-like binding of that scope              |
| `properties`       | properties every node of the kind decodes with, as a JSON object                        |

```zig
.each => .{
    .type = "EachStatement",
    .fields = &.{ "item", "list", "body[]" },
    .block_scope = true,
    .lexical_bindings = true,
},
```

`each (item of list) { ... }` then decodes as `{ type: "EachStatement", item, list, body: [...] }`, with `item` bound in the statement's own scope. Parts that are standard syntax, such as a declaration or an expression, are standard nodes and analyze as they always do.

## What comes free

| Part                                   | With a dialect's nodes                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Semantic analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) | scopes and bindings follow each shape, names inside dialect nodes resolve, and early errors run around them |
| [Traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/)         | every mode walks dialect nodes, with `enter_dialect` and `exit_dialect` hooks                               |
| [Codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/)            | standard nodes print as always, and dialect nodes through `print`                                           |
| [Comments](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#comments)      | attach to dialect nodes as to any node                                                                      |
| [JavaScript](#javascript)              | dialect nodes decode in their shapes, walk, analyze, and print in `yuku`                                    |

A dialect lowers its nodes to standard ones with a transform pass of `exit_dialect` hooks, after which every tool reads plain JavaScript.

## Printing

An optional `print` writes the dialect's nodes back to source, so codegen prints a whole tree.

```zig
pub fn print(w: *dialect.Printer, kind: Node, children: []const ast.NodeIndex) dialect.Error!void
```

| Call           | Does                                               |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `write(code)`  | write code, spaced from what precedes it if needed |
| `space()`      | write a space in the pretty format                 |
| `node(index)`  | print any node, standard or the dialect's          |
| `block(items)` | print a list of statements between braces          |
| `tree()`       | read the tree                                      |

Without `print`, codegen reports a diagnostic for each dialect node it meets.

## JavaScript

A dialect runs in JavaScript as a custom WebAssembly build of Yuku with the dialect compiled in, which `addWasm` builds.

```zig
// build.zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{ .dialect = b.path("src/pipeline.zig") });
b.installArtifact(@import("yuku").addWasm(b, yuku, "pipeline"));
```

`zig build` writes `zig-out/bin/pipeline.wasm`. Ship it in your package, and pass it to `yuku` as the `wasm` option of `parse`, `analyze`, or `new Analyzer`.

```js
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { parse as yukuParse } from "yuku";

const wasm = new WebAssembly.Module(readFileSync(new URL("./pipeline.wasm", import.meta.url)));

export function parse(source, options) {
  return yukuParse(source, { ...options, wasm });
}
```

A browser compiles it with `await WebAssembly.compileStreaming(fetch(url))` instead.

A file whose `path` ends in an extension in `files` parses with the dialect, in the language that entry names, and a source with no `path` parses as the first entry. Any other file, or one given a `lang`, parses as standard syntax, so one build reads a whole project.

A dialect node decodes in its shape, `{ type: "PipelineExpression", left, right, start, end }`. [`yuku/ast`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#js-walking) walks it by its fields, and [`yuku/analyzer`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/#javascript) resolves the names inside it. [`yuku/codegen`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/#javascript) prints them through its [`print`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/#js-printing-new-nodes) option, with the same calls as the Zig printer.

For TypeScript, declare your nodes in `DialectNodes`, which adds them to `Node`, so visitors and `node.type` checks know them.

```ts
import type { BaseNode, Expression } from "yuku/types";

declare module "yuku/types" {
  interface DialectNodes {
    PipelineExpression: BaseNode & { type: "PipelineExpression"; left: Expression; right: Expression };
    TopicReference: BaseNode & { type: "TopicReference" };
  }
}
```

## Cost

A parser built without a dialect has no dialect code, since every position sits behind a compile-time check. With one compiled in, a source that does not opt in pays one flag check per position, and one that does pays one call.

# Testing

Source: https://yuku.fyi/testing/

Yuku is tested for spec conformance, exact AST shapes, codegen soundness, name resolution, and behavior under memory pressure.

## The parser test suite

The parser runs against [parser-test-suite](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/parser-test-suite), over 55,000 tests from [Test262](https://github.com/tc39/test262), the [TypeScript](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript) compiler, and [Babel](https://github.com/babel/babel), synced with upstream daily.

| Category   | Expectation                                                          |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pass`     | Parses with no diagnostics, and the AST matches a snapshot exactly   |
| `fail`     | Produces a syntax error                                              |
| `semantic` | Parses, then fails semantic analysis with an early error             |

The snapshots come from an independent parser, [Oxc](https://oxc.rs), and must match down to every field, position, and comment. Passing files must also walk in source order and pass semantic analysis without a false positive. Yuku passes every test, with zero failures and zero AST mismatches.

The suite runs through the `yuku` package built from local source, so every run checks the whole chain from the Zig parser to the JavaScript AST.

## Codegen

Every parseable file in the suite is printed under several option sets. Each output must parse again, plain output must reparse to the same AST, and printing must be a fixed point with no comment lost or duplicated. The Zig and JavaScript printers must agree byte for byte, and every identifier in a source map must trace back to its original name and position.

## Semantic analysis

Every file in the suite is analyzed, along with real codebases pinned to a commit, such as the TypeScript compiler, Node.js, Vue, and three.js. The TypeScript checker must resolve every reference, values and types alike, to the same declaration Yuku does. [@typescript-eslint/scope-manager](https://typescript-eslint.io/packages/scope-manager) must agree on every runtime reference and write, and on every declaration and its scope. Each runs over a million comparisons.

Each codebase is also linked as one project, and every import, re-export, exported name, and relative path must resolve as in a TypeScript program.

## Fuzzing

A fuzzer throws millions of adversarial inputs at the parser in every language mode, with out-of-memory failures injected along the way. The parser must never crash, and any failure dumps a self-contained reproducer. With everything in one arena, a parse has nothing to leak even when memory runs out.

## Running the suites

```bash
bun run test
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) to run one suite or add cases.

# Security

Source: https://yuku.fyi/security/

Yuku processes source code that may be attacker controlled, so it treats every input as untrusted.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue. Report privately through GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/security/advisories/new), or email [arshadpyaseen@gmail.com](mailto:arshadpyaseen@gmail.com).

We aim to acknowledge reports within 72 hours. Please allow a reasonable window for a fix before public disclosure, and we are glad to credit you in the advisory. Fixes ship against the latest version.

## Our practices

- **No third-party dependencies.** The npm package has no dependencies and runs no install scripts.
- **Provenance publishing.** Releases publish to npm with provenance through OIDC trusted publishing, with no long-lived tokens.
- **Hardened CI.** Every action is pinned to a commit hash, workflow tokens are read-only by default, and the workflows are checked by [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor) and [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://securityscorecards.dev).
- **Reproducible builds.** Installs use a frozen lockfile, and the Zig build has no dependencies.
- **Memory safety.** A parse allocates everything in one arena, and the npm package runs Yuku as WebAssembly, sandboxed from host memory.
- **Fuzzing.** Millions of adversarial inputs per run, see [Testing](https://yuku.fyi/testing/#fuzzing).
